newsitem.title: INDIA: India needs high savings to achieve growth target.
newsitem.headline: India needs high savings to achieve growth target.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Thursday India has to raise its savings and investment rate to achieve seven percent annual growth as targeted in the five-year plan starting on April 1, 1997.
India's Planning Commission, the apex plan panel, targeted seven percent growth in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for the ninth plan, from 1997 to 2002.

"It requires higher rates of investment, higher rates of savings from both domestic and foreign sources and greater efficiency and productivity from the investments," Chidambaram told a meeting of the National Development Council, which includes all of India's state chiefs.

"All of these require policy measures which involve hard political decisions that we must take in the interests of the country and the people, particularly the poor," Chidambaram said in a speech made available to Reuters.
He said the government had to evolve policies which would encourage investment in both private and public sectors.
The ninth plan aims at increasing domestic savings to 26.2 percent from about 24 percent of GDP in the eighth plan.
"That will still leave a gap of 2.4 percent of GDP between our domestic savings and the high rate of investment we must achieve to sustain 7.0 percent growth of the economy," Chidambaram said.
He said this would require a 14 to 15 percent annual growth in exports and a large increase in foreign investment.
"Above all, we need adequate and efficient use of infrastructure services in power, roads, railways, ports, irrigation, telecommunications," Chidambaram said.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda told the meeting the government was committed to taking responsibility for improving infrastructure.
"The most pressing constraint to the achievement of fast and equitable growth is the inadequacy and poor state of the infrastructural sector," Deve Gowda said.
